**Finding: COMPLIANT (sits at/above the fallback) — no redline proposed.**

**What I inspected**
- Article X (§10.1 Ownership, incl. the joint-technology allocation at 10.1(a)–(c)), §10.5 Trademarks
- Article III (§3.1 grant to Sanofi, §3.2 licence back to RevMed, §3.3 retained rights, §3.4 sublicensing/subcontractor assignment, §3.6 no implied licences)
- Definitions: Program Inventions (1.83), Joint Program Technology (1.55), Sanofi/RevMed Sole Program Technology (1.103–1.110), RevMed Licensed Technology (1.99), Field (1.36), Licensed Territory (1.58)
- §6.2 Regulatory Approvals assignment; Article XII effects of expiration/termination (12.3(b)–(c)); Article XIII title reps (13.2(c), (n), (r); 13.3(c))

**Why compliant**
1. **Vendor retention of its own IP** — §3.3 lets RevMed keep everything not expressly licensed. That is the permitted fallback retention.
2. **Our licence** — §3.1 is exclusive (even as to RevMed), covers Research/Develop/Manufacture/use/sell/Commercialize/exploit, in a Field meaning "any and all uses" and a Licensed Territory meaning "all countries and territories of the world"; §3.4(b) allows multi-tier sublicensing; §12.3(b) makes it "fully paid up, royalty free, perpetual and irrevocable" on expiration.
3. **Direction of ownership** — nothing of ours is assigned to RevMed. Third-party inventions assign to the *engaging* Party (10.1(a)); we own Sanofi Sole Program Technology and the Product Marks; and §6.2 assigns Regulatory Approvals *to us*. The Article XII assignments run only on termination and are the ordinary reversion consequence.
4. **Joint ownership** — present, so preferred is not met, but §10.1(b) confers exploitation and licensing "without a duty of accounting or any obligation to seek consent," plus a perpetual, irrevocable, fully-paid, worldwide, sublicensable ex-US licence "for any and all purposes." An unrestricted right to exploit means this is not walk-away.
5. **RevMed's licence in our technology** — §3.2 is confined to "solely to the extent necessary for RevMed to perform its obligations under this Agreement," i.e. delivery-only, with no independent exploitation.

**Noted in the rationale, not redlined:** joint (rather than sole) ownership; the royalty-bearing and terminable character of the licence during the Term (that is the Article IX payment bargain, not an IP-direction defect); and the narrow §3.4(b) consent gate on sublicensing substantially all US rights.
